review_candidates.title: Vice President for Enrollment & Student Affairs
review_candidates.description: Classification: Student Affairs Reports to: AIU President About The American International University American International University (AIU) is a private institution in Kuwait, founded in 2019, offering undergraduate programmes in Engineering and Computing, Architecture and Design, Business, Arts and Sciences, and Education, delivered in English on the American model of higher education. AIU serves a community of more than 3,000 students and is implementing the RISE Strategy 2026–2030, a five-year institutional transformation anchored in research development, WSCUC international accreditation, student success, employability, and community engagement. Enrollment and student success are central to AIU's continued growth and institutional effectiveness. The University seeks to build an integrated student lifecycle model that attracts appropriately qualified students, supports successful transition and engagement, improves persistence and graduation, and provides a high-quality campus experience. The Vice President for Enrollment & Student Affairs provides executive leadership for this agenda and ensures that enrollment strategy and student services are aligned with AIU's academic mission, regulatory obligations, financial sustainability, and RISE priorities. For more information, visit: www.aiu.edu.kw Division Profile The Enrollment & Student Affairs Division oversees admissions, enrollment, registration, student affairs, engagement, student care, athletics, and student well-being. The Division works closely with Academic Affairs and key administrative units to support an integrated student-success experience. The Vice President provides strategic leadership for the Division, ensuring strong service standards, accountability, regulatory compliance, data quality, and continuous improvement across the student lifecycle. Scope of Work The Vice President for Enrollment & Student Affairs (VP-ESA) provides strategic and operational leadership across the student lifecycle, from recruitment and admission through enrollment, student experience, retention, and graduation. The VP-ESA leads strategic enrollment management and student affairs operations, using data-informed planning to support enrollment, student success, retention, regulatory compliance, and effective resource management. The role also ensures a high-quality and integrated student experience across relevant services and functions. As a member of the University’s Executive Leadership, the VP-ESA advises the President on enrollment trends, student success, retention risks, regulatory matters, capacity needs, and emerging opportunities. The position also contributes to institutional strategy, accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and University-wide planning. The VP-ESA works closely with Academic Affairs and the Schools while maintaining clear responsibility for enrollment and student-service operations and respecting academic decision-making authority. Key Responsibilities Strategic Enrollment Management Develop and implement a comprehensive multi-year strategic enrollment management plan aligned with AIU's mission, RISE Strategy, approved academic portfolio, capacity, and financial model. Establish annual and multi-year enrollment targets for new, continuing, transfer, international, and, as programmes are introduced, graduate students, with clear KPIs and accountability. Lead enrollment forecasting, scenario planning, market analysis, competitor analysis, demand modelling, and conversion analysis to inform institutional decisions. Oversee the full recruitment funnel from enquiry and application through admission, deposit, registration, and enrollment, identifying and addressing points of attrition. Develop yield and conversion strategies appropriate to Kuwait and the wider regional market, using evidence from historical trends, student behaviour, and campaign performance. Work with the VPAA and Deans to align recruitment priorities with approved programmes, academic capacity, staffing, facilities, and strategic programme growth. Provide the President and Executive Leadership with regular enrollment dashboards, forecasts, risks, and recommended actions. Admissions, Recruitment & Enrollment Operations Provide executive leadership for Admissions & Student Recruitment, ensuring fair, transparent, timely, and consistently applied admissions processes. Ensure admissions practices comply with Private Universities Council (PUC), Ministry requirements, University policies, approved programme criteria, and applicable accreditation expectations. Strengthen domestic and international recruitment through outreach, partnerships, events, and digital channels. Partner with Branding & Communications on enrollment marketing and applicant communications. Establish service standards and turnaround times across admissions and enrollment processes. Coordinate scholarships and recruitment incentives within approved policies and authorities. Ensure effective transfer processes, with academic credit decisions referred to the appropriate academic authorities. Registration, Systems & Enrollment Analytics Provide executive oversight for Registration & Systems Analytics, ensuring efficient registration operations, accurate student records, reliable enrollment reporting, and high-quality student service. Work closely with the VPAA, Registrar/registration leadership, Deans, and academic units to align registration demand with course availability, approved capacities, progression requirements, and academic policies. Monitor registration patterns, waitlists, credit loads, programme demand, section utilisation, and progression risks, escalating academic matters to the VPAA and relevant Dean for decision. Ensure that registration and enrollment systems support accurate degree progression, prerequisite enforcement, student status, and institutional reporting. Strengthen data governance, data integrity, reporting definitions, and reconciliation across admissions, enrollment, registration, finance, and institutional effectiveness systems. Partner with the Chief Information Officer and relevant system owners to improve Banner/ERP, CRM, self-service, dashboards, workflow automation, and the overall digital student journey. Student Affairs, Engagement & Campus Experience Provide executive leadership for Student Affairs and ensure a coherent, inclusive, student-centred campus experience aligned with AIU's educational mission. Oversee student engagement, clubs, events, student government, athletics, well-being, counselling, and case management. Ensure effective orientation, transition, and student-support programs. Establish clear service standards, referral pathways, and case-management processes. Oversee fair, consistent, and confidential student conduct processes. Promote student voice, participation, and feedback. Drive continuous improvement using engagement, satisfaction, well-being, and impact data. Ensure student well-being and counselling services follow appropriate professional, ethical, safeguarding, confidentiality, and referral standards. Student Success, Retention & Graduation Partnership Lead Enrollment & Student Affairs’ role in retention, persistence, and graduation strategies in partnership with Academic Affairs, Schools, Advising, Registrar, and Institutional Effectiveness. Use student data to identify trends, at-risk populations, and areas requiring intervention. Coordinate Early Alert and Student Success processes, ensuring effective case management and follow-through. Partner with Academic Affairs to address academic and student-service barriers appropriately. Monitor withdrawal, stop-out, re-enrollment, and progression trends and recommend evidence-based interventions. Support timely graduation clearance while respecting the academic authority of the Schools, Registrar, and VPAA. Compliance, Accreditation & Institutional Effectiveness Ensure compliance across the Division with applicable Kuwait regulations, PUC requirements, University policies, privacy requirements, and relevant accreditation standards. Contribute actively to WSCUC accreditation and institutional self-study by providing reliable evidence relating to enrollment, student services, student engagement, retention, student success, and co-curricular effectiveness. Work with Quality Assurance & Institutional Effectiveness to establish measurable outcomes and assessment cycles for Enrollment & Student Affairs programmes and services. Ensure each major student affairs programme or service maintains clear objectives, evidence of effectiveness, and documented improvement actions. Prepare an annual Student Affairs Effectiveness Report and other executive reports required by the President, Executive Leadership, or governing bodies. Maintain appropriate records, audit trails, risk controls, and documented procedures across the Division. Financial Stewardship, Leadership & Institutional Partnership Align enrollment planning with financial forecasts, scholarship strategy, and institutional capacity in collaboration with Finance. Manage the Division’s budget and ensure resources support strategic priorities and measurable outcomes. Lead, develop, and evaluate the Division’s teams, fostering accountability and service excellence. Build strong partnerships across academic and administrative units. Represent AIU with external stakeholders, including government and regulatory bodies, as appropriate. Lead strategic initiatives assigned by the President and contribute to Executive Leadership decisions. Minimum Qualifications Education Earned doctoral degree (PhD, EdD, DBA, or equivalent terminal degree) from an accredited institution. Degree in Higher Education Administration, Enrollment Management, Student Affairs, Education, Business Administration, or a closely related field is preferred. Experience Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in higher education, with significant responsibility for enrollment, admissions, student affairs, student success, or related functions. Proven success in strategic enrollment planning and achieving measurable enrollment, retention, or student-success outcomes. Experience leading complex teams, managing institutional change, and using data and analytics for executive decision-making. Strong cross-functional experience with academic, finance, marketing, institutional effectiveness, and IT teams. Experience with regulatory compliance, accreditation, and institutional effectiveness. International or multicultural higher education experience; GCC experience is highly desirable. Technical & Professional Knowledge Strong knowledge of strategic enrollment management, admissions, recruitment, retention, and the student lifecycle. Comprehensive understanding of student affairs, engagement, wellbeing, conduct, and student support services. Proficiency in student information systems, CRM platforms, enrollment analytics, and data-informed planning. Knowledge of registration, student records, progression monitoring, and academic governance interfaces. Understanding of accreditation and institutional effectiveness, with WSCUC experience highly desirable. Knowledge of enrollment forecasting, tuition revenue, scholarships, financial planning, and resource management. Skills, Competencies & Personal Attributes Executive-level strategic leadership with the ability to translate institutional priorities into measurable outcomes. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and evidence-informed decision-making skills. Excellent communication, negotiation, presentation, and stakeholder-engagement skills. Proven ability to build effective partnerships across academic and administrative units. Student-centred leadership with sound judgement, fairness, discretion, and high ethical standards. Ability to lead through influence, manage competing priorities, and establish accountability across complex functions. Strong financial, operational, and organizational management capabilities. Cultural intelligence and the ability to work effectively in an international university environment in Kuwait. Preferred Qualifications Previous service as a Vice President, Vice Chancellor, Vice Provost, Associate Vice President, Dean, or comparable senior leader with substantial enrollment and/or student affairs responsibility. Demonstrated record of significant enrollment growth while maintaining academic quality and improving retention or graduation outcomes. Experience integrating enrollment management and student affairs into a coherent student-lifecycle strategy. Experience with WSCUC or a comparable US regional accreditation framework. Experience with Banner or comparable student information/ERP systems and modern enrollment CRM platforms. Experience in Kuwait or the GCC and familiarity with PUC requirements. Experience leading organisational redesign, digital transformation, or service improvement in enrollment and student affairs. How to Apply Interested candidates should visit the Job Opportunities section on our website and submit a resume and cover letter via: https://aiu.edu.kw/careers/jobs Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. The successful candidate is expected to commence employment immediately.

review_candidates.title: UN Women: Deputy Director, Policy, Programme and Intergovernmental Division (PPID), D-1 FTA - Nairobi, Kenya
review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. The Policy, Programme and Intergovernmental Division (PPID) is responsible for coordinating and driving the delivery of UN Women’s development results under the Strategic Plan (SP) 2026–2029 through integrated intergovernmental, policy, programmatic and UN‑system support. PPID provides strategic direction, high‑quality substantive and technical guidance, data, knowledge and political analysis to Headquarters, regional and country offices across development, humanitarian, peace and security contexts. The Division leads UN Women’s engagement in global intergovernmental processes, supports Member States in upholding and translating international gender equality norms and standards into national laws and policies, and coordinates UN‑system thematic leadership on gender equality and women’s rights. PPID also plays a central role in results‑based management, knowledge management and organizational transformation, enabling coherent, effective and accountable delivery of UN Women’s mandate. Under the general direction and broad strategic guidance of the Director PPID, and with significant delegated authority, the Deputy Director is accountable for (1) Providing strategic leadership for the planning and implementation of the Division’s strategy and delivery of the Strategic Plan results; (2) Ensuring SP development results coordination, monitoring and accountability at the global level; (3) Providing corporate stewardship of a knowledge management framework for development results; (4) Leading PPID’s engagement in corporate governance mechanisms and corporate initiatives; and (5) Leading the day-to-day executive management of the Division and its compliance with corporate policies and procedures, and (6) Providing leadership for Directorate workplanning, resources and personnel. The Deputy Director works in close collaboration with all HQ Divisions and Regional offices and supervises 5 staff within the PPID Directorate and directly oversees the Political Analysis and Programme Development Unit, the Trust Fund to End Violence Against Women. The Deputy Director consults the Director on matters with institution-wide strategic, reputational or politically sensitive implications. Key Functions and Accountabilities: Provide Strategic Leadership for Divisional Planning and Delivery of UN Women Strategic Plan Results Provide strategic leadership for the formulation, implementation and periodic review of the Division’s Strategic Note, ensuring clear strategic direction, prioritization and alignment with UN Women’s Strategic Plan and corporate commitments. Oversee the coherence, integration, quality and strategic relevance of PPID’s policy, programme and intergovernmental work, ensuring that divisional priorities effectively position UN Women as a global leader on gender equality and women’s empowerment. Ensure that global programming frameworks, corporate policy inputs and strategic guidance developed under PPID translate intergovernmental mandates and emerging policy priorities into actionable, high-impact results at global, regional and country levels. Ensure strategic interconnection between PPID Directorate and Regional Office leadership and timely support of PPID to country and regional offices, especially for crisis response. Exercise delegated authority to ensure quality assurance, strategic oversight and risk management of PPID-led global and cross-thematic initiatives, including those involving multiple divisions and country and regional offices, and support strategic resources mobilization for divisional priorities. Provide senior strategic guidance to the Political Analysis and Programme Development Unit to ensure forward-looking political analysis informs corporate decision-making, risk mitigation and organizational positioning. Represent the Director, as delegated, in high-level intergovernmental, inter-agency and external forums, including with Member State delegations, and senior officials of multilateral institutions, advancing UN Women’s strategic policy and programmatic priorities. Ensure Strategic Plan Development Results Coordination, Monitoring and Accountability at the Global Level Provide strategic leadership for the coordination, monitoring and consolidation of Strategic Plan development results, ensuring organizational accountability, learning and evidence-informed management action including in collaboration with SPRED. Oversee the establishment and institutionalization of global mechanisms that enable systematic tracking, analysis and synthesis of Strategic Plan results across outcomes, impact areas and thematic priorities. Provide strategic oversight to global Outcome and Impact Leads and Indicator Managers to ensure coherence, analytical rigor and alignment across results frameworks, including the identification of risks, bottlenecks and corrective actions. Lead, in partnership with relevant Divisions such as SPRED and DCA, the strengthening of corporate systems and capacities for results reporting, performance analysis and strategic communications to governing and oversight bodies and external audiences. Ensure the provision of high-quality strategic briefs and analytical inputs to inform senior management decision-making, governance deliberations and external accountability processes. Consult the Director on matters where results reporting has institution-wide strategic, reputational or governance implications. Provide Corporate Stewardship of Knowledge Management for Development Results Establish institutional standards and determine corporate priorities for the development and implementation of UN Women’s knowledge management strategy related to development results, ensuring it supports organizational learning, innovation and impact. Champion a culture of evidence-based decision-making, ensuring that evaluations, research, data and lessons learned systematically inform policy positions, strategic choices and programme adjustments across the organization. Oversee the establishment of corporate governance arrangements, quality standards and accountability mechanisms for knowledge products and platforms, clarifying institutional roles, incentives and performance expectations across headquarters, regional and country offices. Ensure that knowledge generation and dissemination under PPID contributes to UN Women’s global normative leadership and supports Member States and partners with timely, credible and policy-relevant evidence. Lead the Day-to-Day Executive Management of the Division Act on behalf of the Director to provide strategic oversight of PPID’s day-to-day management, ensuring operational coherence, compliance with corporate policies, and delivery of divisional priorities. The incumbent is accountable for the Division’s operational performance and delivery against agreed results. Oversee integrated planning, budgeting and resource management across the Division, ensuring alignment between strategic priorities, workplans, staffing and available resources, and proactively managing organizational and delivery risks. Establish and sustain an effective divisional rhythm of business, promoting clear decision-making structures, cross-sectional coordination, accountability and transparent internal communication. Advise the Director on organizational, structural and process improvements, and lead divisional change and transformation initiatives to enhance effectiveness, agility and institutional resilience. Lead PPID’s Engagement in Corporate Governance and Organization-wide Initiatives Represent the Division, as delegated, in corporate governance, oversight and coordination mechanisms such as the Business Review Committee and its Technical Review Group, Risk Management Committee, ICT Board, etc., contributing to organization-wide strategic, policy and management decisions. Provide executive oversight of Trust Funds for which UN Women serves as Secretariat, exercising delegated authority to commit resources and represent UN Women in Trust Fund governance bodies, as assigned. Ensure PPID’s strategic engagement in donor assessments, consultations, roundtables and other corporate resource mobilization and accountability processes. Strengthen strategic collaboration with other UN Women divisions and external partners, including Member States, UN system entities, civil society and regional bodies, to advance coherent delivery of UN Women’s mandate. Provide Leadership for Directorate Workplanning, Resources and Personnel Provide overall leadership and accountability for the Directorate’s bi-annual workplans, annual reporting and performance against agreed objectives. Exercise delegated authority for financial and human resource management, ensuring sound application of internal controls, effective stewardship of resources and compliance with UN Women and UN regulations. Lead and model an inclusive, respectful and high-performing work culture, promoting teamwork, staff development, talent management and accountability for results. Ensure effective performance management of personnel under supervision, including coaching, feedback and compliance with organizational performance management standards. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent leads a team of 9, which includes 5 direct reports (3 P4s, 1 P3, 1 P1). The incumbent also supervises the Chief of Political Analysis and Programme Development Unit (P5) and the Chief of the Trust Fund to End Violence Against Women (P5). Competencies : Core Values: Integrity; Professionalism; Respect for Diversity. Core Competencies: Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues; Accountability; Creative Problem Solving; Effective Communication; Inclusive Collaboration; Stakeholder Engagement; Leading by Example. Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework: Functional Competencies: Deep knowledge of strategy development and implementation, design of performance management systems of goals, targets and monitoring processes; Demonstrated strength in systems thinking, structured problem solving and strategic business planning, with the ability to synthesize disparate information and critically analyze development challenges; Adept at project management, including critical path thinking, setting priorities and planning, particularly in a resource-constrained setting. Ability not only to establish priorities but also to adhere to priorities in a thoughtful way; Strong experience in driving Change Management processes within large, complex development organizations, including the ability create an enabling work environment; Excellent people management and team building skills. Skilled at growing teams through maturity stages (e.g. start-up to establishment). Ability to bring a “coach” mindset to teams, with demonstrated capacity to indirectly leverage human resources and to guide teams to effectively achieve clear, yet complex goals and objectives; Demonstrated negotiating, cultural sensitivity and diplomatic skills; Skilled in group problem solving and collaboration to resolve problems with complex concepts in a dynamic setting; Strong interpersonal, and communication skills; Ability to fluidly switch from strategic to tactical tasks; A highly cultivated sense of resilience: ability to accept and recover from setbacks, to be flexible and adjust to changing circumstances; Ability to leverage information technology, executive information systems, management techniques and tools for optimal office performance; Strong knowledge of UN Women’s mandate of gender equality and women empowerment. Recruitment Qualifications: Education and Certification: Master’s degree or equivalent in international development, public administration, public policy or other relevant social science fields is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. review_candidates.title: Rollout Program Manager
review_candidates.description: Context and role purpose CEO Coaching International is introducing BIG Intelligence to augment its coaching services and support its evolution into a technology-enabled services business. The platform includes three modules: Client, Coach, and Firm. Each will require ongoing rollout support as capabilities expand, alongside the introduction of new CEOCI services. This is a permanent, full-time position. The initial assignment is the phased client rollout from Alpha, planned for November 2026, through Beta, Early Access, and General Availability, currently targeted for May 2027. The role builds and executes the operating plan that prepares clients, coaches, and internal teams to use and support the platform. After the initial launch, the role continues to manage operational rollouts across all three modules and new services. This includes repeatable readiness, enablement, onboarding, communications, and support handoffs for an ongoing software release cadence of approximately every two to three weeks. The level of rollout activity should match the impact of each release; larger capabilities and services may require coordinated launch programs. Role scope and accountability The Rollout Program Manager (RPM)’s primary responsibility is to own the integrated rollout execution. This includes overseeing the launch plans, dependencies & milestone. The RPM will also help assess, identify and mitigate operational readiness, risk management, and escalations. The RPM will also coordinate functional deliverables and secure commitments from their owners. The RPM sits within the Client Success Organization, reporting to the Chief Client Officer. The CCO and Client Success organization own ongoing client adoption, customer experience, and support. Within this context, the RPM coordinates rollout enablement and support readiness, monitors results, and drives follow-through with accountable owners. It may challenge readiness, recommend delaying or resequencing deployment, and escalate unresolved issues. Final decisions remain with designated functional and executive owners. The RPM is NOT responsible for the following: Product vision, strategy, roadmap, requirements, feature prioritization, product acceptance, and release scope remain with the Chief Product Officer and Product Management. Positioning, messaging, differentiation, go-to-market strategy, and launch communications remain with Product Marketing under the CPO. Engineering and AI leadership own technical delivery, quality, security, reliability, and technical readiness. Working relationships The RPM works closely with the CPO, Product Management, Chief AI Officer, Engineering, internal and outsourced development teams, Product Marketing, L&D, Client Success, support, participating coaches, and Firm module process owners. Core responsibilities Integrated rollout planning Maintain one operating plan across platform modules and new services, with clear owners, milestones, dependencies, capacity needs, risks, and decisions. Coordinate initial launch phases and ongoing releases, using repeatable and automated workflows where practical. Operational readiness and expansion Translate approved product scope and service plans into readiness requirements for onboarding, training, communications, user participation, and support. Gather functional readiness evidence and present recommendations on deployment timing and expansion. Keep product release readiness distinct from operational rollout readiness. Coach adoption and organizational change Coordinate coach onboarding, training, office hours, and practical guidance for incorporating BIG Intelligence into coaching relationships. Develop early coach champions with L&D and Client Success, capture evidence of successful use, and identify resistance or workflow barriers that need action. Client and Firm onboarding Coordinate participant selection, rollout waves, access setup, onboarding, and feedback collection with the appropriate owners. Integrate platform onboarding into new coaching-client onboarding. Work with internal process owners to prepare Firm users for new capabilities and changes to their work. Release enablement and communications Coordinate Product Marketing, Product, and L&D deliverables so guidance, approved messaging, and training are ready when needed. Match enablement effort to the scale of the change and coordinate larger launches when appropriate. Feedback and support coordination Use Product’s established intake and classification process for defects and usability issues. Coordinate visibility and handoffs across product issues, training gaps, and adoption barriers without creating a parallel product backlog. Track unresolved issues and ensure clear ownership and user follow-through. Scalable support readiness Coordinate support workflows, knowledge resources, escalation paths, service expectations, and internal or third-party capacity. A designated internal software customer success/support owner manages support operations, vendor performance, and escalated case follow-through. Engineering and AI own technical diagnosis and fixes. Measurement and continuous improvement Maintain a concise scorecard covering readiness, activation, repeat use, coach participation, user feedback, support demand, and unresolved issues. Agree measures and targets with functional owners, compare rollout cohorts, and drive corrective actions. Transfer routine delivery tasks to operational owners while retaining responsibility for future rollout coordination and process improvement. What success looks like Launch phases and ongoing rollouts have clear owners, measurable readiness criteria, and credible plans. Leadership receives reliable evidence for deployment and expansion decisions. Coaches, clients, and Firm users receive timely enablement and support; recurring rollout processes operate consistently and fit the release cadence. Adoption and value measures inform action. Product owns product value and capabilities; Client Success owns ongoing client adoption and success; Firm process owners own internal business outcomes. Required experience At least five years in software program management, implementation, launch operations, or a closely related role, with direct accountability for delivery across multiple functions. Taken at least two software products or substantial releases from a controlled pilot or Beta into broader customer availability, with concrete examples of personal ownership and results. Managed rollout work beyond development delivery, including onboarding, training, communications, support readiness, and adoption. Built practical processes in entrepreneurial software environments where workflows, responsibilities, and organizational capabilities were still developing. Coordinated recurring SaaS releases and organizational change, including enablement and onboarding that continue after the initial launch. Managed senior stakeholders and competing priorities, securing commitments and resolving dependencies without direct reporting authority. Used customer feedback and operational data to adjust rollout plans, with examples of difficult decisions, corrective action, and lessons learned. Required skills Program execution and judgment. Identify the critical path, clarify ownership, resolve delivery risks, and make evidence-based readiness recommendations. Technical fluency. Understand release cycles, testing, environments, defects, integrations, access management, and incident escalation sufficiently to coordinate decisions with technical owners. Adoption and change management . Introduce new workflows into established professional relationships, coordinate training, develop champions, and address barriers to sustained use. Operational design and analysis. Build usable, scalable workflows; automate repeatable steps where appropriate; interpret activation, repeat use, support demand, and cohort performance. Executive communication and influence. Provide concise updates on progress, risks, required decisions, and accountable owners. Challenge readiness constructively and surface disagreements early. Hands-on execution . Run onboarding sessions, organize feedback, validate user workflows, prepare operational guidance, and solve practical rollout problems. Preferred experience Introducing software into a professional services or relationship-driven business; launching AI-enabled products; supporting executive users; building customer success, support, or enablement processes; launching new services; and coordinating small internal teams with outsourced development or support partners. Education and hiring emphasis Bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, computer science, operations, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience (required). Relevant program management, Agile, Scrum, or change management certifications (preferred) An advanced degree is not required.
